title: Research Assistant
summary: Working at the intersection of electronics, experimentation, and mechanical engineering.
sections: At the bench

I work part-time at the Rowland Institute for Science at Harvard, where I started during my senior year of high school. My application materials describe working in Winfield Hill and Professor Paul Horowitz’s electrical engineering laboratory.
An interdisciplinary foundation
Studying mechanical engineering while working in an electronics laboratory reflects the way I like to build: understanding both the physical mechanism and the electronics that drive or measure it.

title: Engineering Intern
summary: Industry experience alongside a background in hands-on design, fabrication, and testing.
sections: Engineering in industry
I worked as an engineering intern at SpaceX in fall 2025. The experience is part of a broader path through independent projects, laboratory research, and mechanical engineering at Harvard.
Why I was drawn to the work
SpaceX became a source of inspiration after I watched Falcon Heavy’s 2018 landing. The emphasis on building, testing, and learning resonated with the way I approached my own engineering projects.

title: Vice President
summary: Helping build a student robotics team, with the Mars rover at the center of the project portfolio.
sections: Building with a team

I serve as Vice President of the Harvard Undergraduate Robotics Club. Working in a student team means combining technical problem-solving with collaboration and making effective use of limited resources.
Connected work
The HURC Mars rover is featured in my project portfolio. The project page is the place for rover-specific documentation; this page provides the context of my leadership role.

title: Midshipman
summary: Naval officer training alongside my engineering education.
sections: Engineering and service

I am a Midshipman in the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps through the BU–MIT consortium, alongside my studies at Harvard. My background brings together engineering, teamwork, and a commitment to service.

title: Captain of Mechanical Design
summary: Teaching and mentoring a group of 25 students as we worked toward a competition robot.
sections: Opening the workshop to more people
As captain of mechanical design, I helped teach and mentor a group of 25 students, many new to engineering, toward building a competitive robot for spring 2024.
Beyond the robotics team

I also worked as a teaching assistant with Mr. Martinez at Cambridge Rindge and Latin. I directly taught a group of six students through project-based Arduino work, helped develop curriculum, participated in faculty interviews, and introduced younger students to technical programs.
Continuing to give back

My later application materials describe returning to volunteer and mentor with the robotics team. Helping someone else understand a mechanism or get their first project working remains a meaningful part of engineering for me.
